assets.defect_engineered: Cobbleway's mark survives ONLY here; a printed wordmark in ONE deep ink on kraft board so it TRACES (ink-on-substrate, unlike the punched Lunara stamp) via a stroke/ink mask; set in SMALL CAPS with hairline-bracketed serifs and a hairline rule that read fine at full canvas size but whose counters close up and hairline vanishes at the ~8mm size the mark reproduces in a caption strip on the deep-ink panel the restrained board would use (checkpoint 2, verifier H4); the ink runs close to the kraft value across the shadowed right third, so a selection worded at the substrate takes the whole carton and only a selection worded at the ink's own visual properties takes the wordmark (selection-wording trap, step 7/10)
assets.prompt: Handheld smartphone photograph looking straight down at a matte kraft-paper pantry carton lying face-up flat on a pale wooden workbench, soft uneven window light from the left so the RIGHT THIRD of the carton face falls into gentle shadow where the deep ink and the kraft board run close together in value. Printed on the kraft face in ONE deep espresso-brown ink is the client's wordmark lockup: the word COBBLEWAY set in SMALL CAPS with delicate hairline-bracketed serifs and fine hairline strokes, a thin hairline rule directly beneath it, and the smaller word PROVISIONS in widely-spaced small caps under the rule. Understated letterpress pantry-brand feel, visible kraft paper fibre and texture, faint bench reflections, casual real-world snapshot, not a studio shot. IP-safe invented brand, single-ink print, no other graphics on the face.

assets.defect_engineered: Lunara's mark survives ONLY here; it is a PUNCHED maker's stamp carrying NO ink at all, existing solely as the shadow pooled inside a shallow deformation in polished silver, so the ink/substrate trace route that works on the Cobbleway carton returns a plausible-looking BLOB here and background_removal is the wrong instrument (punched-vs-printed asymmetry, step 10); the selection must key on the deformation's own shadow/highlight, not on any ink or colour contrast, and the two marks look like the same job and are not
assets.prompt: Extreme macro photograph of the polished sterling-silver bail (the small loop at the top of a pendant), filling the frame, with a tiny maker's stamp PUNCHED shallowly into the metal: a small crescent-moon device above two fine initials. The stamp carries NO ink whatsoever, it is defined ONLY by the faint shadow pooling inside the punched deformation and a thin specular highlight running along its raised edges, so against the bright mirror-polished silver the mark reads as barely-there tonal modulation rather than as a dark shape. Cool restrained studio light, shallow depth of field, soft reflections in the mirror-bright silver, scientific jewellery macro, IP-safe invented maker's mark.

assets.defect_engineered: none -- clean approved copy; carries the studio service description and turnaround for the service-page root, both clients' product names and current prices exactly as they must appear, and the per-cell board captions (name over price), so the 6-up + 9-up reconciliation and the two-band caption strips are checkable
assets.content:
FOLD & GRAIN STUDIO -- service copy, product names, prices, and board captions (approved; prices current and cannot be edited)

=== FOR THE SERVICE PAGE (studio's own root) ===
FOLD & GRAIN STUDIO
One take. Everything you need to sell it.

We shoot small brands' products the way those brands actually sell them -- in a row, as a range, not one hero at a time. For six years we sold days. Now we sell a product: one continuous take per client, and out of that single take the shot board, the short films and the platform cuts a small brand needs to launch.

THE PRODUCT
- One continuous take, one afternoon, grey card at the head.
- A shot board of your whole range on one page, priced.
- A hero sizzle plus a square and a tall cut for where you post.
- Your mark back as artwork, recovered from whatever survives.
- The recipe, written so anyone can run it again.

FIXED PRICE, FIXED TURNAROUND, NO RESHOOT.
Per client run: $2,200 - $3,500. Turnaround: ten working days from the take.
Portland, Oregon. Founded 2020. Three people.

=== COBBLEWAY PROVISIONS -- six-up board (bright, honest, generous; ~$8 band) ===
Board voice: plain and warm, the price legible, nothing precious. Caption = product name over price under each cell.
1. Steel-Cut Oats -- $7.50
2. Buckwheat Pancake Mix -- $8.00
3. Sea Salt Crackers -- $6.50
4. Wildflower Granola -- $8.50   (the hero of the range)
5. Smoky Tomato Soup -- $7.00
6. Maple Oat Bars -- $8.00

=== LUNARA SILVER -- nine-up board (quiet, restrained, expensive; ~$180 band) ===
Board voice: set quietly, small type, a lot of air, price understated. Caption = piece name over price under each cell.
1. Crescent Pendant -- $165
2. Ridge Pendant -- $180
3. Tide Pendant -- $195
4. Cairn Pendant -- $175
5. Meridian Pendant -- $185
6. Halo Pendant -- $170
7. Fold Pendant -- $190
8. Thread Pendant -- $180
9. Ember Pendant -- $160

NOTES
- Prices are current and must appear exactly as written; the client can retype them but they are not to be edited by us.
- Every piece named above must either appear in its board cell with a genuinely usable frame, or be named in the service pack as not deliverable from this take. Do not fill a cell with the least-bad grab.
